description: Declarative coverage/rule registry for the bounded marine-technical entailment contract. Every controlled enum token in the fixed v0.6 field inventory (plus the preserved legacy v0.5 rig_type/rudder_type vocabularies) is classified as exactly one of DEFINITIONAL_ENTAILMENT, DIRECT_ONLY or NO_DERIVATION. This is a closed, hand-maintained coverage table, not a generic rule engine: adding a new schema enum token without adding its classification here is a coverage failure, by design. This file's own 'schema'/'enum_path' metadata and 'classifications' array are informational/self-descriptive only -- the controlling contract tests independently hardcode the expected field->schema-location mapping and the allowed classification set, and cross-check this file against that independent expectation rather than trusting it as its own authority (see tests/contract/test_marine_technical_entailment.py).

value.meaning: Exact positive value assertion: the target field's true value IS this literal (enum token, integer, or the sentinel string 'unknown').

relation.meaning: Inclusive lower-bound assertion for an integer target field only (values used in v0.1: '>=1', '>=2'). The target field's true value is at least N; the exact value beyond that bound is not asserted and must not be silently upgraded to one.

excludes_value.meaning: Negative assertion for an enum target field: the target field's true value is NOT this one specific token. No other value is positively asserted.

not_concrete.meaning: Negative assertion for a free-text target field: the target field must not carry any concrete (non-null) value. Used only when a paired qualified count fact (e.g. centerboard_count=0) structurally forecloses any concrete descriptor existing -- driven by a positive qualified fact, not an inference from the free-text field's own absence.

conditional.meaning: A closed, single-purpose piecewise output reserved exclusively for the one already-accepted SLICE-0034 twin/rudder_count case (rule MTE-LEGACY-RUD-006). v0.1 does NOT generalize this into a conditional-output mechanism for other rules; a second rule wishing to use it would require an explicit accepted decision, not a routine registry edit.

STANDARD_MTE_GUARD_V0_1.description: The single, uniform qualification/applicability/conflict guard shared by every DEFINITIONAL_ENTAILMENT rule in this v0.1 registry. It restates MARINE_TECHNICAL_ENTAILMENT.v0.1.md section 4's mandatory epistemic rules as machine-checkable structured fields rather than free-form prose. Every rule below references this same policy by id; no rule in v0.1 defines a weaker, stronger, or rule-specific guard.

reverse_relations.reason: A concrete hull_count does not uniquely identify a named topology: an allowed 'other' topology (e.g. a proa-like asymmetric configuration) can share the same hull_count as monohull/catamaran/trimaran. Reverse of MTE-HULL-001..003 is unsafe and is not authorized.

appendages.keel_type.notes: No non-board keel_type token (full/modified_full/long_fin/fin/wing/bulb/twin/bilge/swing/lifting/shoal) entails centerboard_count=0 or daggerboard_count=0: keel-centerboard and other hybrid appendage combinations exist, and absence is not negative evidence.

appendages.keel_subtype.reason: Arbitrary string; no closed vocabulary exists to bind an entailment to.

appendages.centerboard_type.reason: Arbitrary string; no closed vocabulary exists to bind an entailment to.

appendages.daggerboard_type.reason: Arbitrary string; no closed vocabulary exists to bind an entailment to.

appendages.rudder_position.notes: rudder_position never entails rudder_support in v0.6-native data: a transom-positioned rudder can independently carry keel/skeg support semantics (see BOAT_DESIGN_V05_TO_V06_MAPPING.md section 3.2 and fixtures/technical_profile/valid/01_classic_aft_cockpit_masthead_sloop.json).

appendages.rudder_support.notes: rudder_support never entails rudder_position (independent axes) and never entails keel_type/skeg_type concretely beyond the skeg-presence exclusion in MTE-RUD-002.

appendages.skeg_type.notes: skeg_type=full and skeg_type=partial do not entail rudder_support=skeg: a skeg-equipped hull can still carry a rudder the skeg does not structurally support.

rig.sailplan.notes: sailplan never entails masthead_fractional in v0.6-native data, including sailplan=cat: an unstayed cat rig is a plausible basis for masthead_fractional=not_applicable, but that basis is a maritime-exception judgment call outside the v0.6 token itself, so it is deliberately NOT asserted here (see MARINE_TECHNICAL_ENTAILMENT.v0.1.md section 6).

rig.masthead_fractional.notes: masthead_fractional never entails sailplan or mast_count: masthead/fractional character is not uniquely restricted to one sailplan family.

reverse_relations.reason: mast_count=1 does not uniquely identify sloop/cutter/cat; mast_count=2 does not uniquely identify ketch/yawl/a two-masted schooner. Reverse of MTE-RIG-001..006 is unsafe and is not authorized.

rig.rig_variant.reason: Arbitrary string; no closed vocabulary exists to bind an entailment to.

deck.helm_type.notes: helm_type never entails helm_count: a wheel or tiller helm does not definitionally guarantee a specific helm station count (twin-wheel installations exist).

legacy.rig_type.notes: Positive rows (masthead_sloop/fractional_sloop/cutter/ketch/yawl/schooner/cat_rig) preserve the accepted SLICE-0034 compatibility mapping (BOAT_DESIGN_V05_TO_V06_MAPPING.md section 3.1) verbatim. 'other' and 'unknown' are classified NO_DERIVATION in this entailment contract, consistent with the universal sentinel rule applied to every other field in this registry: an opaque escape token or an absent-information sentinel authorizes no cross-field truth. This does NOT change or weaken the pre-existing, separately-tested BOAT_DESIGN_V05_TO_V06_MAPPING.md compatibility table itself (tests/contract/test_boat_design_v05_to_v06_mapping_conservatism.py, unchanged) -- that table's 'other'->'other'/'unknown'->'unknown' rows remain valid v0.5->v0.6 *shape/field-renaming* migration semantics (moving a value from the old field name to the new one), which is a different concern from this contract's *truth-entailment* classification. A structural field-rename is not, by itself, a substantive cross-field MTE entailment, so no MTE-LEGACY-RIG rule exists for 'other'/'unknown'.

legacy.rudder_type.notes: Positive rows preserve the accepted SLICE-0034 compatibility mapping (BOAT_DESIGN_V05_TO_V06_MAPPING.md section 3.2, amendments 1 and 2) verbatim, including the rudder_balance-is-always-unknown finding and the twin/rudder_count conflict rule. 'other' and 'unknown' are classified NO_DERIVATION here for the same reason given for legacy.rig_type above: they are v0.5->v0.6 shape/field-renaming migration facts (unchanged, separately tested), not substantive MTE cross-field truth entailments.

rules.prerequisites: hull_configuration is a qualified, accepted (non-provisional, non-conflicted) value of exactly 'monohull'.
rules.applicability: Applies within the single resolved BoatDesign baseline or NamedVariant/DesignOption override scope where hull_configuration is itself qualified as monohull; does not import hull_configuration from a different scope.
rules.exceptions: None: a monohull has exactly one hull by definition.
rules.conflict_behavior: If the same scope already carries a qualified explicit hull_count other than 1, surface UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT per TECHNICAL_PROFILE_SPEC.v0.1.md sections 5-6; do not silently overwrite either value. (Also independently enforced structurally by BOAT_DESIGN_SCHEMA.v0.6.json's hull_configuration/hull_count if/then invariant when both fields are concretely present.)
rules.evidence_basis: Dictionary/definitional meaning of 'monohull' (single-hulled vessel); already-accepted v0.6 schema invariant.
rules.lineage_requirement: Derived hull_count must record rule_id MTE-HULL-001, version 0.1, the qualifying hull_configuration=monohull fact and its applicability scope, distinguishable from a directly reported hull_count.

rules.lineage_requirement: Derived hull_count must record rule_id MTE-HULL-002, version 0.1, the qualifying fact and applicability scope.

rules.prerequisites: keel_type is a qualified, accepted value of exactly 'centerboard' (i.e. the boat's primary keel-equivalent appendage is itself a centerboard).
rules.applicability: Applies within the single resolved BoatDesign baseline or NamedVariant/DesignOption override scope where keel_type is itself qualified.
rules.exceptions: The exact count is not guaranteed (single or twin centerboards both exist); only presence of at least one is definitionally guaranteed.
rules.conflict_behavior: If the same scope already carries a qualified explicit centerboard_count of 0, surface UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT; do not silently overwrite either value.
rules.evidence_basis: Internal HullQ controlled-vocabulary identity, not external maritime research: the v0.6 keel_type enum value's own literal word is 'centerboard' (BOAT_DESIGN_SCHEMA.v0.6.json), which is the same controlled word the schema uses to name the corresponding appendage-count field's subject (centerboard_count). If the boat's own primary keel-equivalent appendage IS a centerboard, at least one centerboard must exist. This is the same class of reasoning already accepted in SLICE-0034 for masthead_sloop/fractional_sloop (BOAT_DESIGN_V05_TO_V06_MAPPING.md section 3.1): the source token's own word is the entailed fact's subject.
rules.lineage_requirement: A derived centerboard_count>=1 fact must record rule_id MTE-KEEL-001, version 0.1, the qualifying keel_type fact and applicability scope; it must not be upgraded to an exact count without separate qualified evidence.

rules.conflict_behavior: If the same scope already carries a qualified explicit daggerboard_count of 0, surface UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT; do not silently overwrite either value.
rules.evidence_basis: Internal HullQ controlled-vocabulary identity, not external maritime research: the v0.6 keel_type enum value's own literal word is 'daggerboard' (BOAT_DESIGN_SCHEMA.v0.6.json), the same controlled word the schema uses to name the corresponding appendage-count field's subject (daggerboard_count). Same class of reasoning as MTE-KEEL-001 and the accepted SLICE-0034 masthead_sloop/fractional_sloop word-identity precedent.
rules.lineage_requirement: A derived daggerboard_count>=1 fact must record rule_id MTE-KEEL-002, version 0.1, the qualifying keel_type fact and applicability scope; it must not be upgraded to an exact count without separate qualified evidence.

rules.prerequisites: rudder_support is qualified as exactly 'skeg'.
rules.applicability: Applies within the single resolved BoatDesign baseline or NamedVariant/DesignOption override scope where rudder_support is itself qualified.
rules.exceptions: Does not determine whether skeg_type is 'full' or 'partial'; only excludes 'none'.
rules.conflict_behavior: If the same scope already carries a qualified explicit skeg_type of 'none', surface UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT; do not silently overwrite either value. Also independently enforced structurally by the v0.6 schema's skeg_type=none/rudder_support=skeg mutual-exclusion invariant.
rules.evidence_basis: A skeg-supported rudder definitionally requires an existing skeg. This exclusion is driven by a positive qualified fact (rudder_support IS 'skeg'), not by any absence -- it must not be confused with inferring negative facts from missing/unknown data.
rules.lineage_requirement: Record rule_id MTE-RUD-002, version 0.1, and the qualifying rudder_support=skeg fact.

rules.prerequisites: skeg_type is qualified as exactly 'none'.
rules.applicability: Applies within the single resolved BoatDesign baseline or NamedVariant/DesignOption override scope where skeg_type is itself qualified.
rules.exceptions: Does not determine what rudder_support actually is (keel/free/transom/other/unknown); only excludes 'skeg'.
rules.conflict_behavior: If the same scope already carries a qualified explicit rudder_support of 'skeg', surface UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT; do not silently overwrite either value. This is the symmetric reverse direction of MTE-RUD-002, recorded independently per the 'direction by direction' completion requirement, and is likewise already enforced structurally by the v0.6 schema.
rules.evidence_basis: Absence of any skeg definitionally means the rudder cannot be skeg-supported. Driven by the positive qualified fact skeg_type IS 'none' (a concrete reported value), not by skeg_type being missing/unknown -- 'none' is a reported absence-of-skeg fact, which is different from an unreported/unknown skeg_type.
rules.lineage_requirement: Record rule_id MTE-RUD-003, version 0.1, and the qualifying skeg_type=none fact.

rules.prerequisites: sailplan is a qualified, accepted value of exactly 'sloop'.
rules.applicability: Applies within the single resolved BoatDesign baseline or NamedVariant/DesignOption override scope where sailplan is itself qualified.
rules.exceptions: None: a sloop is by definition single-masted.
rules.conflict_behavior: If the same scope already carries a qualified explicit mast_count other than 1, surface UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT; do not silently overwrite either value.
rules.evidence_basis: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'sloop' (https://www.britannica.com/technology/sloop, retrieved 2026-08-30): 'a single-masted sailing vessel with fore-and-aft rigging, including mainsail, jib, and sometimes one or more headsails.' A sloop is single-masted by definition, directly supporting mast_count=1.
rules.lineage_requirement: Record rule_id MTE-RIG-001, version 0.1, and the qualifying sailplan=sloop fact and applicability scope.

rules.prerequisites: sailplan is a qualified, accepted value of exactly 'cutter'.
rules.applicability: Applies within the single resolved BoatDesign baseline or NamedVariant/DesignOption override scope where sailplan is itself qualified.
rules.exceptions: None: a cutter is by definition single-masted (distinguished from a sloop by headsail plan, not mast count).
rules.conflict_behavior: If the same scope already carries a qualified explicit mast_count other than 1, surface UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT; do not silently overwrite either value.
rules.evidence_basis: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'cutter' (https://www.britannica.com/technology/cutter-sailing-craft, retrieved 2026-08-30): a cutter is 'a small, speedy sailing vessel similar to a sloop... a single mast rigged fore and aft, carrying a mainsail and at least two headsails.' Single-masted by definition, directly supporting mast_count=1.
rules.lineage_requirement: Record rule_id MTE-RIG-002, version 0.1, and the qualifying sailplan=cutter fact and applicability scope.

rules.prerequisites: sailplan is a qualified, accepted value of exactly 'cat'.
rules.applicability: Applies within the single resolved BoatDesign baseline or NamedVariant/DesignOption override scope where sailplan is itself qualified.
rules.exceptions: None: a cat-rigged vessel is by definition single-masted (one mast, one sail, no headsail/forestay).
rules.conflict_behavior: If the same scope already carries a qualified explicit mast_count other than 1, surface UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT; do not silently overwrite either value.
rules.evidence_basis: Merriam-Webster, 'catboat' (https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/catboat, retrieved 2026-08-30): 'a sailboat with a single mast set far forward and a single large sail with a long boom.' A cat-rigged vessel is single-masted by definition, directly supporting mast_count=1.
rules.lineage_requirement: Record rule_id MTE-RIG-003, version 0.1, and the qualifying sailplan=cat fact and applicability scope.

rules.prerequisites: sailplan is a qualified, accepted value of exactly 'ketch'.
rules.applicability: Applies within the single resolved BoatDesign baseline or NamedVariant/DesignOption override scope where sailplan is itself qualified.
rules.exceptions: None: a ketch is by definition two-masted (main and mizzen forward of the rudder post; the mizzen-position distinction from a yawl does not change the mast count).
rules.conflict_behavior: If the same scope already carries a qualified explicit mast_count other than 2, surface UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT; do not silently overwrite either value.
rules.evidence_basis: Britannica Dictionary, 'ketch' (https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/ketch, retrieved 2026-08-30): a ketch is defined as a two-masted sailing vessel. Two-masted by definition, directly supporting mast_count=2.
rules.lineage_requirement: Record rule_id MTE-RIG-004, version 0.1, and the qualifying sailplan=ketch fact and applicability scope.

rules.prerequisites: sailplan is a qualified, accepted value of exactly 'yawl'.
rules.applicability: Applies within the single resolved BoatDesign baseline or NamedVariant/DesignOption override scope where sailplan is itself qualified.
rules.exceptions: None: a yawl is by definition two-masted (main and a smaller mizzen aft of the rudder post -- the mizzen-position distinction from a ketch does not change the mast count).
rules.conflict_behavior: If the same scope already carries a qualified explicit mast_count other than 2, surface UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT; do not silently overwrite either value.
rules.evidence_basis: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Yawl' (https://www.britannica.com/technology/yawl, retrieved 2026-08-30): a yawl is a two-masted sailing vessel whose mizzenmast is stepped aft of the rudder post, distinguishing it from a ketch (whose mizzen is stepped forward of the rudder post). Two-masted by definition, directly supporting mast_count=2.
rules.lineage_requirement: Record rule_id MTE-RIG-005, version 0.1, and the qualifying sailplan=yawl fact and applicability scope.

rules.prerequisites: sailplan is a qualified, accepted value of exactly 'schooner'.
rules.applicability: Applies within the single resolved BoatDesign baseline or NamedVariant/DesignOption override scope where sailplan is itself qualified.
rules.exceptions: The exact mast count is not guaranteed: two-masted schooners are typical but three-or-more-masted schooners exist. Only the lower bound of 2 is definitionally guaranteed.
rules.conflict_behavior: If the same scope already carries a qualified explicit mast_count of 0 or 1, surface UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT; do not silently overwrite either value.
rules.evidence_basis: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'schooner' (https://www.britannica.com/technology/schooner, retrieved 2026-08-30): 'a sailing ship rigged with fore-and-aft sails on its two or more masts.' The source itself states 'two or more', which is exactly why only the lower bound (>=2), not an exact count, is authorized here.
rules.lineage_requirement: Record rule_id MTE-RIG-006, version 0.1, and the qualifying sailplan=schooner fact and applicability scope; the bound (>=2) must not be silently upgraded to an exact count without separate qualified evidence.

rules.prerequisites: Legacy v0.5 rudder_type is qualified as exactly 'twin'; source rudder_count is jointly known (including the qualified null state).
rules.applicability: Applies to translating a single qualified v0.5 record's own baseline into v0.6-shaped facts; both rudder_type and rudder_count must come from the same record/scope.
rules.exceptions: rudder_position, rudder_support and rudder_balance are explicitly NOT entailed by 'twin' (must project 'unknown' for all three): 'twin' describes rudder count only.
rules.conflict_behavior: A source rudder_count concretely other than 2 (e.g. 0, 1, 3, 4) is an internally inconsistent v0.5 payload. This rule does not silently overwrite the recorded count with 2, and does not silently keep the recorded count while dropping the twin fact; it raises a flagged conflict for manual/conflict resolution per TECHNICAL_PROFILE_SPEC.v0.1.md sections 5-6, exactly mirroring the existing accepted RudderCountMappingConflict behavior.
rules.evidence_basis: BOAT_DESIGN_V05_TO_V06_MAPPING.md section 3.2 'rudder_count and twin' (accepted SLICE-0034 mapping, amendment 2): the word 'twin' definitionally IS the count fact, so a null/unrecorded source count must not discard it.
rules.lineage_requirement: Record rule_id MTE-LEGACY-RUD-006, version 0.1, the qualifying legacy rudder_type=twin fact, and the source rudder_count value actually observed (null/2/conflict).
